methods.description: Identify the actual order of two operations, then apply their inverses to both sides in reverse order, including negative numbers and a multiplication/division pair.
For a grouped sum or difference, undo multiplication or division outside the grouping before undoing addition or subtraction inside.
Expand a single bracket by multiplying every inside term, then undo addition or subtraction and multiplication to solve without collecting extra pronumeral terms.
Check a proposed equivalent-equation step by applying the operation to both sides and every term when multiplying or dividing.

sourceReview.locator: Solve two-step equations with negative coefficients: 3-2x=15 and -4-x/2=3; guided practice and Key Ideas

This supports negative coefficients as a signed-number case of inverse operations, rather than adding an advanced equation method.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted 3-2x=15 to 5-3x=26 in workedExamples[1], giving -7 by division by -3. Retained the existing negative grouped quiz task and rewrote all of its distractors to match specific incorrect operations. sourceReview.locator: Identify outside/inside inverse operations; Solving Two-Step Equations involving Grouping paired examples 3(x+1)=15 and (x+3)/2=5; guided practice and Key Ideas
sourceReview.observation: Read the outside-first rule, operation diagrams, complete grouping examples, guided practice and Key Ideas. A bracket is grouping; the outside multiplication or division is undone before the addition or subtraction inside. The fraction bar groups the whole numerator.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted 3(x+1)=15 to 4(x+3)=52 in workedExamples[3]. Combined the ordinary fraction-bar and grouped numerator examples into the contrasting pair x/4+6=9 and (x+6)/4=9 in workedExamples[5]; these are different placements, not different numerical cases. Corrected the theory claim that a bracket itself is the last operation. Replaced (x+4)/3=2 with (x+5)/3=4 so the solution is not coincidentally equal to the right-hand side.

sourceReview.locator: Solve equations with brackets: left worked example 3(x+4)=21 and Key Ideas allowing divide-first or expand-first; right example and harder guided cases explicitly outside this skill
sourceReview.observation: The left worked example multiplies every inside term, then subtracts the expanded constant and divides the coefficient. The adjacent Key Ideas explicitly allow dividing first or expanding first. The right worked example adds another pronumeral term, so its expand-and-collect scope is not permission to extend this two-operation skill.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted the left worked example to 4(x+5)=23 in workedExamples[4], retaining expansion and an exact fraction at the final line. Replaced mastery 4(x-5)+4x=20 and quiz 3(x+4)+5x=44 with single-bracket tasks 5(x-7)=38 and 5(x+7)=23. Preserved each question position, quiz ID and mastery marker; explicitly required expansion where it is the assessed method.

sourceReview.locator: Mixed Practice: Example Solve equations of up to two steps, first row 4x/7=-12 with multiply-by-7 then divide-by-4 working
sourceReview.observation: The complete worked example applies multiplication by the denominator followed by division by the coefficient, retaining an equation at each line. The adjacent Your Turn items use the same two-operation multiplication/division approach.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted 4x/7=-12 to 5x/3=17 in workedExamples[2], with exact result 51/5. Replaced the shortcut-friendly mastery equation 147x/13=1470 with 7x/4=19, exact answer 76/7, so equal factors do not hide the two operations.

sourceReview.locator: Equivalent Equations: Multiplying every term; unbalanced/balanced image5.png and image6.png; paired multiplication/division example and Key Ideas
sourceReview.observation: Read the every-term rule, paired complete equivalent-equation examples and Key Ideas, and visually inspected both balance images. The unbalanced image doubles only the x tiles; the balanced image doubles both the x tiles and all unit tiles on both sides. This directly supports diagnosing a next step which leaves a constant unchanged.
sourceReview.adjustments: Adapted the equivalent-equation teaching into workedExamples[6], checking the claimed x+3=55 step from x/5+3=11 against x+15=55. Used different numbers and a question about an incorrect step, not a copied published practice card. Repaired the existing incorrect-next-step quiz numbers and made all option reasons explicitly distinguish equivalent steps from the one invalid step.

Replaced three out-of-scope assessed equations: development[7] required three inverse operations; mastery[1] and quiz.q8 required expanding and collecting an additional pronumeral term.
